title: Why We Watch at All
sentences: I have spent an unreasonable proportion of my adult life watching other people run.
The result of any single match changes nothing whatsoever in my actual daily life.
That argument has never once reduced my interest by any genuinely measurable amount.
Part of the appeal is surely that the outcome of the thing remains truly unknown.
Very little else in adult life offers uncertainty in such a neatly contained form.
There is also the ordinary pleasure of belonging to a crowd that wants one thing.
I am suspicious of that feeling and enjoy it enormously at exactly the same moment.
The players themselves now have almost no connection with the town they represent.
We support a name, a colour and a long series of borrowed collective memories.
Understanding all of this has never once persuaded me to stop going on Saturdays.
